Build output does not travel between homes.
A refresh that rewrites the unit around it does not delete it.
A unit the agent committed in still blocks the teardown.

ticket.found_by: running a worktree's own tooling once, on three real repositories
ticket.model_change: None, and the reason is recorded rather than left implicit. The claim is about WHICH BYTES a reconciliation owns; sync_body is a total function over SyncPaths in which every path is content by construction. Expressing it needs a second, disjoint path class and multiplies the axis this slice was already decomposed to control -- for a property decided by one predicate over path NAMES. Covered end to end instead.
ticket.objective: Running `discover.py` in a ticket worktree -- the thing a worktree exists to do -- writes `skills/test-graph/project_sdk_sources/build-logic/.gradle/**` and `scripts/__pycache__/*.pyc` INSIDE a unit. Those moved the unit's digest, so `home close-out` returned `conflicted` with a non-actionable remedy ("... then resolve: executionHistory.bin, ..."), the printed remedy run verbatim exited 1 without clearing the gate, and `home sync --merge` then reported that nothing was written. The unit stayed unreconciled forever. Authorship confirmed by timestamps: 6, 5 and 5 files across three repositories. A built jar (validation-graph-build-logic-0.1.0.jar) was separately carried worktree -> project by a merge as though it were somebody's work. `home clone` had skipped these names inside a unit since the first clone. ChildHomeMaterializer never asked. One name skipped by one caller and not the other is a unit that reports conflicted for good.
ticket.resolution: One definition of re-derivable, dev.skillmanager.shared.util.Rederivable, read by both. It is applied at the top of BOTH walkers, so a skipped path is invisible to the materializer in every direction at once: not fingerprinted, so it cannot make a unit look edited; not copied, so it cannot travel between homes; and NOT DELETED, because carryOverUnownedTrees moves it across the atomic swap. "Not mine to compare" and "mine to destroy" cannot both be true of the same bytes. A directory whose only content is unowned is itself unowned, or the exclusion would fail by exactly one directory level. TWO SCOPES, and the asymmetry is the answer to "shared, derived, or separate". Rederivable.CACHES -- tool-private names that can only be caches -- is shared verbatim with HomeCloner, so its behaviour is unchanged. Rederivable.OUTPUT_ROOTS (build, target, node_modules, .venv, venv) is read by the reconcile ONLY: a clone has to hand over a home that WORKS and re-anchors those trees per copy, and node_modules/<pkg>/build/Release/*.node is a prebuilt native binary nothing on the destination rebuilds; a reconcile has no re-anchoring pass at all, so a .venv it copied would arrive with console-script shebangs naming the SOURCE home. Two questions, one answer where the questions agree. `.git` IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE SET, stated at length in Rederivable's javadoc under an anchor, because it churns exactly like the entries that are and every instinct says to add it. Issue #29: a unit whose agent COMMITTED work holds those commits in .git and nowhere else, so a skipped .git makes the unit read as unmodified, clears the teardown, and takes the commits with it.
